section_summary: A December 11 memorandum forwards a San Francisco customs collector’s December 5 telegram and the Commissioner of Customs’ December 7 reply. The collector asks how to handle Japanese naval vessels, their cargoes, and printed matter; the reply addresses the printed matter’s customs status.

people.name: L. Jeen
people.role: Signer of the memorandum; name uncertain in OCR

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding customs telegram and reply
subfiles.to: Director, Bureau of Navigation and Steamboat Inspection
subfiles.about: Requests advice on instructions to the San Francisco collector concerning Japanese vessels’ entry and clearance.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the collector’s telegram and the December 7 reply, seeking further guidance on entry and clearance.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting instructions on Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Asks how to treat printed matter, oil cargoes, and customs formalities aboard Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The collector seeks instructions on printed matter aboard a naval tanker and on reporting, entry, clearance, and supervision of vessels carrying oil.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning printed matter aboard Japanese vessel
subfiles.about: States that imported printed matter is subject to regular entry and tariff classification.
subfiles.summary: Imported printed matter requires regular customs entry and classification under tariff laws.
